newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Dec 11.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech coalition and the main political parties in Bonn both show satisfaction with the text of the Czech-German declaration, which was publicised on Monday. The Czech opposition Social Democrats seem negative, but have still not stated their clear position.

- The largest Czech banks are showing an urge to slim down and are laying off some of their employees. Komercni Banka plans the largest reduction of about 1,200 workers in 1997 followed by Ceska Sporitelna with plans to lay off roughly 900 employees next year.

- The Slovak National Property Fund has demanded two billion crowns from the Czech National Property Fund as compensation for a possible mutual exchange of shares from Komercni Banka and Vseobecna Uverova Banka.
- Risk capital could fill the gap in investment sources and contribute to the standardisation of the domestic capital market. The major investment will probably be into restructuring businesses.

- The largest Czech electric company CEZ is ready to restart discussions regarding the Organisation for Energy Control (UED). Prague municipal authorities cancelled the control on Monday because the conditions were not agreeable.

PRAVO - Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy, and the Cuban Foreign Trade Minister signed a new trade areement with Cuba yesterday during a conference of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore.
- The Czech company Motoinvest sold its controlling shares in 4. C.S. Holding, which is owned by A-Invest, to Agrobanka's former investment company.

LIDOVE NOVINY - A 10-member team of doctors, led by American heart surgeon professor Robert Ginsberg, will from now on look after President Vaclav Havel's health. Although the president's physical condition before the operation on his lung was considered serious, the doctors confirm that his health has greatly improved.

- Sokolovska Coal (SUAS) has signed a basic medium-term contract until the year 2001 to supply coal to the electric company CEZ. According to the contract, CEZ will take from two to 2.2 million tons of coal yearly, which would mean roughly 600 million crowns a year for SUAS.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The government budget is threatened with a multibillion crown deficit this year due to problems with stabilising the balance of payments and relatively high inflation. The cabinet already cut government spending by 9.3 billion crowns halfway through the year to cut the deficit.
